description: Compensation committee deck proposing FY2027 executive pay design for a public cybersecurity company.
provenance: Modeled on public-company compensation committee materials: peer positioning, pay-for-performance alignment, annual and long-term incentive scorecards, retention risk, dilution, and resolutions. Deliberately exercises an eight-slide deck with a two-series pay-for-performance line chart, percentage-heavy comparisons, and governance-specific approval language.

content.title: FY2027 Executive Compensation Design
content.subtitle: Compensation Committee | November 17, 2026 | Privileged and confidential

content.title: The FY2027 design raises performance leverage and targets retention risk.
content.subtitle: Committee advisor recommendation
prose: Target CEO compensation remains near the peer median; 87% is variable.
Performance stock units deliver 67% of target pay.
Retention awards address vesting gaps for the product and revenue chiefs.

content.title: Realized CEO pay tracks relative shareholder outcomes
content.subtitle: Sentinel Ridge percentile rank within the cybersecurity peer group

content.title: FY2026 design versus proposed FY2027 design
content.subtitle: Changes strengthen performance orientation and simplify measures

content.title: FY2027 incentive scorecards
content.subtitle: Threshold, target, and maximum performance levels
bulletPoints: Annual ARR growth: 16% threshold, 20% target, 25% maximum; 50% weighting
Annual free cash flow margin: 17% threshold, 20% target, 23% maximum; 30% weighting
Strategic: cloud workload protection attach, federal authorization, and leadership succession; 20% weighting
Three-year ARR CAGR: 17% threshold, 20% target, 24% maximum; one-third of PSUs
Three-year cumulative free cash flow: $910M threshold, $1.08B target, $1.27B maximum; one-third of PSUs
Relative TSR: 25th percentile threshold, 50th target, 75th maximum; one-third of PSUs with negative-TSR cap at target

content.title: Retention, dilution, and shareholder considerations
content.subtitle: Targeted actions within the existing equity plan
bulletPoints: Chief Product Officer retention award: $3.2M, 60% performance-based, vesting over three years; replacement risk rated high
Chief Revenue Officer retention award: $2.4M, 50% performance-based; conditioned on FY2027 federal go-to-market milestones
No special award proposed for the CEO, CFO, or Chief Legal Officer
FY2027 burn rate of 2.6% versus 2.8% peer median; overhang declines to 9.4% after the annual grant
Compensation advisor expects the design to score favorably on pay-for-performance alignment and problematic-pay-practice screens
Clawback, double-trigger change-in-control, and no-hedging policies remain unchanged

content.title: Approve the FY2027 program and two retention awards.
content.subtitle: Separate votes under compensation committee agenda items 2, 3, and 4
prose: Awards use the 20-day average share price ending February 12, 2027.
Any increase above 5% requires further committee approval.
